value.name: explains house can be preserved
value.description: The speaker explains that the house has survived debts for generations and can still be kept through financial arrangements instead of being sold.
evidence: It has outlasted every debt anyone in it ever had. It will outlast yours. There are ways. There are second mortgages, and there are equity arrangements, and there are renters in the third-floor apartment, and there are siblings who might, if asked properly, agree to a structure that lets the house stay a house.

value.name: advises consulting lawyer
value.description: He tells Rosa that she already has a lawyer and should ask her about the possible financial structures.
evidence: You have a lawyer. Ask her.
"You can ask her about the structures."

value.name: insists house need not solve everything
value.description: He says the house can remain standing regardless of their unresolved personal issues, as long as it is not sold to someone who would destroy it.
evidence: The other things you will work out yourself, or you will not, and the house will stand regardless.
The house does not require you to work out the other things.
The house requires only that you not sell it to someone who will tear out the kitchen.

value.name: laughs and wipes tears
value.description: He laughs again and wipes his face, revealing an emotional, familiar gesture from his childhood.
evidence: He wiped his face with the back of his hand, which was a gesture she had also seen him do at eleven.

value.name: raises issue of Rosa's room
value.description: He brings up the room mentioned in the document and addresses it directly to Rosa.
evidence: "Rosa," he said. "About the room. About what was in the document. About your room."

value.name: offers separate lifetime room agreement
value.description: He proposes drawing up a personal agreement giving Rosa the room for life, independent of the estate and the house's fate.
evidence: "I would like, if you are willing, to draw up a separate agreement, outside the estate, between you and me personally, that gives you that room for the rest of your life regardless of what happens to the house."
"I would like to do this even if we keep the house."

"I would like to do it because my mother intended it and because the document only operates if we keep the house and I do not yet know whether we will keep the house and I do not want your security to depend on a question that has not been answered."

value.name: asks Rosa to agree
value.description: He asks Rosa whether she will allow him to make the separate agreement.

value.name: Rosa considers proposal silently
value.description: Rosa looks at him for a long time, indicating she is weighing his offer before responding.
evidence: Rosa looked at him for a long time.
